en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Fifth Chapter
Is there a perverted knowledge for one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa absorption? Yes.
Is it a perversion to regard the impermanent as permanent?
One should not say so …pe… [is it a perversion to regard] what is suffering as happiness …pe…?
Is it not the case that to perceive what is non-self as self … and what is unattractive as attractive is a perversion?
It should not be said so … [and so on].
Is it knowledge that is perverted for one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa absorption?
Yes. Is it unwholesome? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it not the case that it is wholesome?
Yes, it is.
If it is wholesome, then indeed you should not say:
"For one who has attained the earth-kasina attainment, there is perverted knowledge.
Is the perversion that takes the impermanent to be permanent unwholesome?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is there, for one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa absorption, a perverted knowledge, and is that unwholesome?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Is it a perversion to perceive what is suffering as happiness …pe… what is non-self as self …pe… and what is unattractive as attractive, and is that unwholesome?
“Yes,” you say.
“Does one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa absorption possess perverted knowledge, and is that unwholesome?
You should not say so … [and so on] … No, indeed.
Is there a perverted knowledge for one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa absorption, and is that unwholesome?
Yes. Is the perversion that takes the impermanent to be permanent wholesome? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … For one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa attainment, is there perverted knowledge, and is that unwholesome? Yes.
Is it a perversion to perceive what is suffering as happiness …pe… what is non-self as self …pe… and what is unattractive as attractive, and is that [perversion] wholesome?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it knowledge of the contrary for one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa attainment? Yes.
"An Arahant could enter into the attainment of the earth-kasina?
"Yes.
"If an Arahant could enter into the attainment of the earth-kasina, then indeed it should not be said—"
“Knowledge regarding what is contrary to one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa absorption.
Knowledge regarding what is contrary to one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa absorption: would an Arahant enter the earth-kasiṇa absorption? Yes.
Is there inversion in an Arahant?
One should not say so… [as before] … Is there inversion in an Arahant?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does the Arahant have a perversion of perception, a perversion of mind, and a perversion of view?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
"There is no perversion of perception, perversion of mind, or perversion of view in an Arahant"?
Yes, [you say].
If there is indeed no perversion of perception, perversion of mind, or perversion of view in an Arahant, then surely you should not say: [that he has such perversions].
“There is perversion in an Arahant.
Should it not be said that for one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa absorption, there is knowledge of the opposite?
“Yes,” you say.
“When one enters the attainment of the earth-kasiṇa, does everything become earth?
You should not say so.
"Therefore, for one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa absorption, there is perverted knowledge.
Is it the case that for one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa absorption, there is perverted knowledge? Yes.
Is it not the case that earth exists, and that there is someone who enters into the attainment of earth as earth?
Yes, it is so.
If earth exists, and if there is someone who enters into the attainment of earth as earth, then indeed, sir, you should not say: [that this is impossible].
“Knowledge is perverted for one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa absorption. [Objection:
Is it not the case that when there is earth, and one enters into the earth as earth, that knowledge is perverted? [Response:
Yes, it is.
"Nibbāna exists; for one entering the attainment of Nibbāna as Nibbāna, it becomes perverted"?
One should not say this...
[as before] ...therefore, it should not be said—
“Knowledge is perverted for one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa absorption.
The Discussion on Perversion is finished.
